'''Coleman Dupont Donaldson''' (September 22, 1922 – August 7, 2009) was a [[Fluid mechanics|fluid physicist]] and [[Aerospace engineering|aeronautical engineer]] who specialized in [[Turbulence|turbulent flow]] and [[computational fluid dynamics]]. He made broad contributions during his career in turbulent transport, supersonic flow, and [[Armour|armor]].<ref name=Bushnell>{{cite book|author1=Bushnell, Dennis M.|title=Memorial Tributes: National Academy of Engineering, Volume 14|date=2011|publisher=National Academy of Engineering|isbn=978-0-309-15218-1|pages=61–65|chapter-url=http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=12884|accessdate=23 December 2014|chapter=Coleman Dupont Donaldson}}</ref>

== Biography ==
In 1942 he received a bachelor's degree from [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]]. Afterwards he worked for the [[National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics]] (NACA) at the [[Langley Memorial Aeronautical Laboratory]].<ref name=Legacy-obituary /> While serving in the [[United States Army Air Corps|Army Air Corps]] in 1945–1946 he was assigned to [[Bell Aircraft]], where he worked on the development of the [[Bell X-1|X-1]] and [[Bell X-2|X-2]].<ref name="Princeton-Alumni-Weekly-memorial" /> Afterwards he worked at NACA again and completed his doctorate at [[Princeton University|Princeton]] under [[Luigi Crocco]] in 1957. He was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1979. He was a member of the [[Du Pont family]] and a grandson of [[T. Coleman du Pont]].<ref name="Bushnell"/>
